newsitem.title: MALAWI: MALAWI SEEKS TO REDUCE BUDGET DEFICIT TO 7.8 PCT.
newsitem.headline: MALAWI SEEKS TO REDUCE BUDGET DEFICIT TO 7.8 PCT.

text.p: Malawi Finance Minister Aleke Banda said in his 1997/98 budget speech on Monday the government hoped to decrease its budget deficit to 7.8 percent from 8.5 percent of Gross Domestic Product in the new financial year.
"The deficit before grants is projected at 3.14 billion kwacha reflecting a decline from 8.5 percent in 1996/97 to 7.8 percent of GDP in 1997/98," Banda said.
He said the government expected to spend 9.79 billion kwacha ($652.9 million) out of which 7.54 billion kwacha would be recurrent and 2.25 billion kwacha will be spent on development.
Banda said an additional 1.78 billion kwacha will be raised through foreign loans and grants.
The deficit including grants of 1.78 million kwacha was expected to increase to 4.3 percent of GDP in 1997/98 from 3.8 percent the previous year, due to an expected decline in foreign loans.
He said the government aimed to achieve real growth of 7.1 percent during its 1997/98 economic programme, compared to 9.5 percent in 1996.
"This far outstrips Africa's average growth in output of five percent in 1996," he said.
Banda said that in efforts to increase revenue import duties on raw materials used in manufacturing would be scrapped and a 10 percent surcharge for the hotel industry cut.
"A 10 percent reduction on hotel industry will be effected in conjunction with this measure to promote tourism," he said.

Banda said corporate tax on export processing zones will be removed completely while new investments of between $5 million and $10 million will be given an option of an indefinite 15 percent tax or a five-year tax holiday.
"New investments in excess of $10 million will be given similar option, but with a tax holiday of 10 years," he said.
